info.title: US Mortgage Calculator API
info.description:
US mortgage calculations and 50-state property tax reference data. Every endpoint is a pure function: the same request always returns the same response, nothing is stored, and no authentication is required for the public tier.

These are estimates built from published averages, not loan offers or rate quotes.

post.description: Full monthly housing cost for a US mortgage: principal and interest, property tax, homeowners insurance, mortgage insurance and HOA dues, plus lifetime totals and payoff timing. Pass a state name to use that state's average property tax rate. This is the right tool for 'what would my payment be on a $400,000 house'.

loanTermYears.description: Loan term in years. Most US mortgages are 15 or 30.

annualInsurance.description: Annual homeowners insurance premium in US dollars.

post.description: Mortgage insurance for any US loan programme, including the upfront charges most calculators omit. Conventional: monthly PMI and the month it cancels at 80% and 78% loan-to-value. FHA: the 1.75% upfront premium, monthly MIP, and whether it runs for the life of the loan or ends after 11 years. VA: the funding fee, tiered by down payment and prior use, and waivers. USDA: guarantee and annual fees.

schema.description: Mortgage insurance for any programme: conventional PMI with its cancellation point, FHA MIP and upfront premium, the VA funding fee, or USDA fees.

post.summary: Work out how much house someone can afford
post.description: Maximum affordable home price from income, existing debt payments and available down payment, using the 28/36 qualifying ratios. Reports which of the two ratios is the binding constraint, which is the actionable part: a buyer limited by the back-end ratio can raise their budget by clearing debt, one limited by the front-end ratio cannot.

schema.description: Maximum affordable home price from income, debts and available down payment.

annualGrossIncome.description: Household income before tax, in US dollars per year.

monthlyDebtPayments.description: Existing minimum monthly debt payments: car loans, student loans, credit card minimums. Excludes housing.

annualInterestRatePercent.description: Annual nominal interest rate as a percentage, for example 6.5 for 6.5%.

loanTermYears.description: Loan term in years. Most US mortgages are 15 or 30.

frontEndRatioPercent.description: Maximum housing cost as a share of gross income. 28 is the conservative standard.

backEndRatioPercent.description: Maximum total debt as a share of gross income. 36 is conservative; lenders often allow 45 and sometimes 50.

post.description: Compares renting and buying on net wealth rather than on monthly payment, accounting for equity, appreciation, maintenance, selling costs, and the return a renter earns on money not spent on a down payment. Returns the year buying overtakes renting. The result is highly sensitive to the appreciation and investment-return assumptions, which are returned alongside it.

post.summary: Compare loan options side by side
post.description: Compares two to five loan scenarios and reports which is cheapest by monthly payment and which by lifetime cost, separately, because they frequently are not the same loan. Use for 15-year versus 30-year, FHA versus conventional, competing lender quotes, or with and without discount points.

schema.description: Compare loan options. Reports the cheapest by monthly payment and by lifetime cost separately, because they often differ.

scenarios.description: Two to five loan scenarios to compare side by side.

label.description: Name for this option, for example "30-year fixed".

post.summary: Look up a state's property tax rules
post.description: How property tax actually works in one state: how assessed value is derived, any statutory growth cap, the billing cycle, named exemptions such as homestead, the filing deadline, who hears appeals and the window to file, notable county variation, and a link to the state's own tax authority. Use this when the question is about mechanics or deadlines rather than a dollar amount.
